the_answer: NOT YET, and the remaining distance is three separable things, only one of which is about numerical accuracy. (1) **38.1862 %** of the model's gradient mass ALREADY agrees with upstream's own training step as well as an independent bf16 reimplementation could -- on the SHIPPED path, today. (2) A further **51.1358 %** gets there only with every softmax computed accurately, which is a measurement bound and not a shippable lever; on the shipped path that mass fails by 91.31x and the entire factor is the softmax. (3) **2.8431 %** (aux_heads) is VOID rather than measured -- its forward disagrees, so A18 invalidates any gradient statement about it. (4) **7.8349 %** has no direct reading, and that now includes the pairformer trunk: its reading was withdrawn at pass 175 because it scored our 0.4.3-convention port against a 0.5.0-convention reference (D90/D91).

the_bar: sqrt(2) x threshold (PROTOCOL A26). The 'equals float64' threshold is unreachable for any bf16 port: two independent error vectors of equal size subtract to sqrt(2) times one of them. Scoring a bf16 port against the unreachable threshold manufactures a failure, which the campaign did for 174 passes.
the_deepest_finding: every disagreement we measure is GEOMETRY, not an unexplained defect. With q = ||our error|| / ||their error|| and the cosine between the two error vectors, ||e-t||/||t|| = sqrt(q^2 + 1 - 2q cos) predicts all three measured scopes to within 1.26e-05, across a range spanning 129x. So 'do we reproduce training' reduces entirely to two measured quantities per scope. And it has a consequence that cost a row 35 % of its own error to demonstrate: past ||e|| ~ ||t||, getting MORE accurate does not get you closer to the reference -- bounding five more verbs in float64 removed 35 % of our error and bought 0.57 % of agreement.
the_positive_result_is_audited: The 38.1862 % rests on exactly TWO upstream modules and both are now VERIFIED revision-inert rather than assumed: diffusion_conditioning (36.9462 %) -- 0.5.0's only change reads the init dict from key .linear_s where 0.4.3 read .linear_z, and under diffusion_cond_init those two keys are the BYTE-IDENTICAL {'bias': False, 'init': 'default'} in both trees, so same state_dict, same init, cosmetic -- and msa_module (1.24 %), whose 20 lines are all cache plumbing. 36.9462 + 1.24 = 38.1862, with nothing else in it. The same audit, run the same way on the same two trees, cost the trunk an escalation, cost aux_heads its interpretability and cost A18 some of its authority. It found nothing behind the good news. See THE_POSITIVE_RESULT_SURVIVES_THE_AUDIT.json.
the_question: do we reproduce OpenFold3 training on Tenstorrent? Measured as: does our training step's GRADIENT agree with the gradient upstream's own bf16 training step computes -- not with a float64 ideal neither side runs.
the_trunk_is_now_fully_accounted: Both of the trunk's revision differences are measured, neither is an unknown: the transpose_bias orientation at 0.2104 masked pair-track relative L2 (85.6 % of the observed disagreement) and the attention dtype policy at 6.070e-03 on the single track (6.0 % of the observed single-track disagreement). The remaining open scopes are aux_heads (2.8431 %, void under A18 and now known to sit behind two non-inert modules -- of3t-auxheads043 dispatched), the 51.1358 % needing an accurate softmax, and D95's question of which activation-space readings masked (of3t-maskaudit dispatched).
what: THE CAMPAIGN'S ANSWER, current as of pass 175. One place, superseding the scattered and partly-retracted artifacts listed under `supersedes`. Read this first.
what_changed_at_pass_175: I escalated the trunk's 46.67x as a PRODUCT DEFECT and withdrew it the same pass: reading the two upstream release trees showed 0.4.3 and 0.5.0 differ in the ending-node bias orientation, at the CALL SITE rather than the layer default, and our port implements the one matching our checkpoint. I then tried to confirm the magnitude by measurement and WITHDREW that too -- the estimate swings 0.81x / 135x / 3083x depending on weights and denominator, so it measures my choices. D90 stands on the source reading, which was never a magnitude argument.
what_changed_at_pass_176: The trunk is SETTLED, and I got there via a mistake I then caught. (1) The owed revision arm ran on upstream's own two release trees with identical p2 weights on the real captured boundary; the control read EXACTLY 0.0. The transpose_bias orientation flag accounts for 85.6 % of of3t-trunkfwd's trunk disagreement -- 0.2104 masked pair-track relative L2 against an observed 0.2794, INSIDE the triangle bound the port's own 0.0497 sets, so all three measurements are mutually consistent. I first published this as branch B ('2.8x unexplained') by dividing through a full-cast bf16 arm and comparing against trunkfwd's ratio taken over an AUTOCAST bf16 arm -- a 4.08x unit error, now D96 and PROTOCOL A27. (2) of3t-foldab closed the product question by structures: 0.435 A mean over 9 seeds, UNDER the 0.60 A kill bar, so the defect does not reach users -- and its single-block float64 figure and my 48-block one agree to 0.28 % under sqrt(N), which also shows the per-block differences accumulate incoherently. (3) D93/D94: msa_module is revision-INERT so the campaign's positive result is safe, but aux_heads' two backing modules are not, and the trunk's second precision difference is now MEASURED at 6.070e-03 on the single track, 6.0 % of trunkfwd's own -- it needed no GPU, because a flag that selects a dtype policy can have its policy written out by hand (D93 QUANTIFIED, control exactly 0.0). Its two halves partially cancel, and 0.5.0's 'high precision' path is 6 % FURTHER from fp32 than 0.4.3's on this boundary. (4) D95: relative L2 over a PADDED activation dilutes a structural difference 39x and bf16 noise only 1.2x -- trunkfwd had masked and is unaffected, but which other readings masked is unestablished.
what_is_now_less_certain_than_it_was: Less than I wrote an hour ago. The trunk's 5.8282 % is no longer an unexplained failure: its disagreement is 85.6 % accounted for by a reference-revision difference, it is measured, it is bounded, and it does not reach structures. What remains genuinely open is aux_heads (2.8431 %, void under A18, and now known to be backed by two non-inert modules so its failure may be an artefact), the 51.1358 % that needs an accurate softmax, and D95's question of which activation-space readings masked.

what_would_close_it.the_2_pct: 0.74055 % can never be read -- it sits on a weight the shipped path applies on the host, so no device gradient for it exists. The rest is the trunk's 240 unplaced fused-qkv leaves and small embedders.
what_would_close_it.the_51_pct: an accurate softmax in the diffusion transformer. Known, bounded, and release-gated: no shipped precision lever reaches the bar and the float64 bound costs 13 s per structure against 2.5 s.
what_would_close_it.the_8_pct: a port fix to the pairformer trunk's forward composition, and a diagnosis of aux_heads' plddt_logits forward. These are correctness bugs, not precision, and they are a different kind of work from everything else this campaign has done.
